title: Sense, Think, Act
description: A washing machine follows the same steps every time. A robot looks first, then decides. That one difference is what this whole course is about.

content.value: The Loop Every Robot Runs
Every robot ever built runs the same three steps, over and over. A ₹2,000 toy robot does it. So does a Mars rover. The robot senses the world, thinks about what it found, then acts.
You are running that loop right now. Your eyes sense these words. Your brain thinks about what they mean. Your hand acts by scrolling down. Then it all starts again.
Here is a real one. Watch it measure the wall, decide, then move. Now drag the wall closer and watch it change its mind.
The three boxes, as real parts

content.value: Sense: how a robot notices
A robot has no eyes or ears. It has sensors. A sensor is a small part that turns something in the world into a number, because a number is the only thing a computer can work with.

👁  camera        → what is in front of me?
📏  distance      → how far away is that wall?
🌡️  temperature   → is it hot in here?
〰️  line sensor   → is the floor black or white?
🎙️  microphone    → did someone say something?
A distance sensor never says "a wall!". It says 23, meaning 23 centimetres. Deciding that 23 is close enough to worry about is a separate job, and it happens in the next step.
Think: how a robot decides
For a robot, thinking means following a rule. A rule looks like this: if the distance is under 20, turn instead of driving forward.
Later in this course you will write these rules yourself, first as blocks you drag, then as real Python. For now you only need the shape of it: a number goes in, a decision comes out.
Act: how a robot changes the world
Acting means changing something in the real world. The parts that do it are called actuators. A motor spins a wheel. A servo swings an arm. A speaker makes a sound. An LED lights up.
A machine that only senses is a thermometer. A machine that only acts is a fan. A robot does all three, in a loop, without anyone telling it what to do each time.
Watch the loop run
Here is a floor-cleaning robot meeting a chair leg. Read it as two full turns of the loop:

SENSE   distance sensor reads 12 cm
THINK   12 is less than 20 → something is in the way
ACT     stop, turn right, drive on

SENSE   distance sensor reads 140 cm
THINK   140 is plenty → the way is clear
ACT     keep driving
Nobody told the robot the chair was there. It found out by itself. That is what makes it a robot.

Here are eight parts from a real robot. Drop each one into the step it belongs to.

content.title: 🧭 Sense, Think or Act?
content.prompt: Every robot part belongs to one of the three steps. Which step does each one belong to?

tasks.label: Camera
tasks.explain: It turns light into numbers the computer can read. That is sensing.

tasks.label: Motor spinning a wheel
tasks.explain: It pushes on the world and makes something move. Parts that do that are called actuators.

tasks.label: The rule 'if distance < 20, turn'
tasks.explain: A number goes in and a decision comes out. That is exactly what THINK means.

tasks.label: Microphone
tasks.explain: Sound comes in and becomes numbers. Nothing has been decided yet, so it is still sensing.

tasks.label: Speaker saying 'hello'
tasks.explain: Acting is not only movement. Making a sound changes the world too.

tasks.label: The controller board choosing a route
tasks.explain: The controller board is where sensor numbers turn into decisions.

tasks.label: Distance sensor reading 23
tasks.explain: It reports the number 23. It has no idea that means "a wall". Working that out happens in THINK.

tasks.label: LED lighting up red
tasks.explain: Something the world can see. A small act, but still an act.

content.value: Key takeaway: a robot senses the world, thinks about what it found, acts, then starts again. These three steps come back in every module of this course.

quiz.question: Your robot's distance sensor reads 8. Which step of the loop has just happened?
options: It has SENSED: a number arrived from the world
It has THOUGHT: it decided something
quiz.explain: A sensor only reports a number. Deciding what 8 means, and then doing something about it, are the two steps that come after.

quiz.question: A toy car drives forward whenever you hold the button, and stops when you let go. Which box is missing?
quiz.explain: It acts, and your finger does the sensing. But it never decides anything for itself, so THINK is what is missing. Your thumb is the brain.

quiz.question: Which of these is an actuator (an ACT part) rather than a sensor?
options: A motor that spins a wheel
quiz.explain: Cameras and microphones bring information in. A motor pushes back out on the world, and that is acting.

quiz.question: Why does the loop go round and round instead of running once?
options: Because the world keeps changing, so the robot must keep checking
Because computers can only count to three
Because it makes the robot go faster
quiz.explain: The world does not hold still. Sensing once at the start would leave the robot blind for the rest of the trip.

quiz.question: A robot vacuum reads 15 cm from the wall ahead. Which line is its THINK step?
options: The number 15 arrives from the sensor
15 is under 20, so something is in the way
quiz.explain: Thinking is the rule that turns a number into a decision. The number arriving is sensing. The wheels stopping is acting.
